grf.observed_anchor: Shared evidence already showed that rebinding the active WAL pathname while leaving main untouched can leave main SQLITE_FCNTL_HAS_MOVED false while the same connection continues a successful transaction.
grf.generated_reality: SQLITE_FCNTL_JOURNAL_POINTER might expose the active WAL sqlite3_file strongly enough that calling that object's xFileControl(SQLITE_FCNTL_HAS_MOVED) detects the sidecar rename missed by the main-file guard.
grf.strongest_counter_reality: The WAL sqlite3_file object's xFileControl(SQLITE_FCNTL_HAS_MOVED) may also return false after a WAL rename/rebind on the tested Unix VFS, so JOURNAL_POINTER plus HAS_MOVED would still not bind WAL filesystem-object history.
grf.discriminator: Ordinary deterministic replay of the already-recorded WAL-sidecar rebind class using a diagnostic extension that obtains SQLITE_FCNTL_JOURNAL_POINTER and invokes the returned sqlite3_file pMethods->xFileControl with SQLITE_FCNTL_HAS_MOVED.

go_unusual_experiment.name: TOCTOU_PATH_REBIND_AROUND_LSTAT
go_unusual_experiment.interpretation: The hypothesized false receipt-inode binding was not reproduced under this injected timing. Do not promote this as a vulnerability finding.

ordinary_followup.name: JOURNAL_POINTER_HAS_MOVED_REPLAY

environment.platform_scope: local Linux container; not accepted Hostinger

ordinary_followup.mechanism: Loadable SQLite diagnostic extension; sqlite3_file_control(main, SQLITE_FCNTL_JOURNAL_POINTER, &journal_file); journal_file->pMethods->xFileControl(journal_file, SQLITE_FCNTL_HAS_MOVED, &moved).
ordinary_followup.intervention_replay: Rename active WAL sidecar and place a distinct decoy file at the original -wal pathname, matching the already-recorded shared counterevidence class.
limitations: No claim that production permissions permit WAL rebinding.
Result rejects only this proposed diagnostic mechanism as sufficient on the tested lane.

primary_source_alignment.sqlite_file_control: SQLite documents sqlite3_file_control as dispatching to the xFileControl method for a database file, with selected opcodes handled directly by core.
primary_source_alignment.sqlite_journal_pointer: SQLite documents SQLITE_FCNTL_JOURNAL_POINTER as returning the sqlite3_file object associated with the rollback journal or write-ahead log for a connection.
primary_source_alignment.sqlite_has_moved: SQLite documents SQLITE_FCNTL_HAS_MOVED as writing whether the nominated file has been renamed, moved, or deleted since it was opened.

architecture_delta.delta: Do not implement a WAL-sidecar acceptance gate that assumes JOURNAL_POINTER plus HAS_MOVED closes sidecar object identity. The productive acceptance path still needs an independently measured object-bound WAL/journal identity or an equivalently strong VFS/FD-bound mechanism, tied to the real connection and operation.
architecture_delta.next_discriminator: Prefer a mechanism that exposes or independently binds the actual OS-backed WAL object for the productive connection without depending on private SQLite VFS layout; then verify a real unique transaction/readback and revalidate across restart/reopen, rollback, downgrade and library-swap controls on accepted Hostinger.
architecture_delta.rollback: No product code was changed; retain current main and existing draft candidates.
